title: SongForge Capacity Thesis
description: Issue #18 AC4: the shape proof for PRD #6 / decision #8 -- sse_connected_listeners rises with the number of connected clients while radio_advances_total and datastore-op counters stay flat, because SSE fan-out is in-process off ONE Redis pub/sub subscription per app instance. Also charts write-path create-rate throughput (AC4b).

panels.title: Connected SSE listeners (independent variable)
panels.description: songforge_sse_connected_listeners -- the value loadtest/connection-ceiling.js drives up. Expected to rise through a k6 ramp.

panels.title: Radio advance rate + pointer-event fan-out (expected FLAT)
panels.description: rate(songforge_radio_advances_total[1m]) and rate(songforge_radio_pointer_events_relayed_total[1m]) -- the thesis's direct observable: these should stay flat regardless of how many listeners are connected, because only ONE leader instance drives the clock-triggered advance and pointer events fan out in-process, not per-listener datastore writes.

panels.title: Datastore-op rate (expected FLAT as listener count rises)
panels.description: rate(songforge_http_requests_total[1m]) broken out alongside job counters -- the datastore-facing request/op volume that should NOT scale with sse_connected_listeners, since a listener holds an in-process SSE connection rather than issuing per-tick datastore reads/writes.

panels.title: Create-rate throughput (write path, AC4b)
panels.description: rate(songforge_jobs_created_total[1m]) vs rate(songforge_jobs_dispatched_total[1m]) -- driven by loadtest/create-rate.js against the simulator seam. The two tracking each other shows the write path sustaining the target create-rate without the queue unboundedly backing up.
